title: Quant bottleneck lighthouse probe - MAY2026
content:
Purpose
This note captures a focused investigation into a recurring throughput anomaly we’ve been seeing on mixed-precision deployments. We call it the "lighthouse" bottleneck because a small subset of kernels periodically dominate latency and fan out tail behavior (like a lighthouse pulse). Goal is to (1) explain observed signal, (2) measure tradeoffs across INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ, (3) propose mitigations we can land quickly in the scheduler/runtime.

Background / motivation
- High-level symptom: 99.9th token latency spikes on multi-tenant dedicated GPU pools when running AWQ and GPTQ variants concurrently. Median throughput looks fine.
- Hypothesis: certain attention/ff kernels compiled for INT8/FP8 have non-linear execution time with sequence length and lane utilization, causing transient kernel saturation and queueing in our local kernel pools. Kernel runtime variance cascades through batching and KV cache reuse, producing tail latency spikes.

Experiment summary (setup)
- Hardware: A5000 nodes (8x A5000), CUDA 12.2, custom kernel set v2.7.
- Models: llama-13b and a trimmed 7B
